title: Production of brain-derived neurotrophic factor and neurotrophin-4 in E. coli
author: Holzner, Böttinger, et al.

steps.title: Prepare LB media
steps.instruction: Make 1.8 L LB (3 × 600 mL in 2 L shaker flasks) for inclusion‑body culture and 50 mL LB in a 250 mL flask for inoculation; autoclave both and cool to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Set up inoculation culture
steps.instruction: Transform plasmid into 100 µL chemo‑competent BL21(DE3) Rosetta 2 cells, recover in 500 µL LB, transfer to 50 mL LB containing 100 µg/mL ampicillin and 20 µg/mL chloramphenicol, and grow overnight at 37 °C, 200 rpm (optional monoclonal colonies can be isolated on LB‑agar with the same antibiotics and grown in 5 mL LB overnight).

steps.title: Prepare buffers and assay
steps.instruction: Prepare all buffers listed in Materials and Equipment; keep urea‑containing buffers fresh at 4 °C to avoid carbamylation. Set up a Bradford assay calibration curve (e.g., with BSA) for protein quantification.

steps.title: Solubilize inclusion bodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend each gram of inclusion‑body pellet in 4–6 mL Solubilization Buffer 2, centrifuge 17 500 × g for 20 min at 20‑22 °C, transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL tube, and determine protein concentration by Bradford (dilute 1:20 or 1:50 if >10 mg/mL; aim for ≥10 mg/mL).

steps.title: Fold by rapid dilution
steps.instruction: Prepare Folding Buffer at 100 × the volume of the solubilized sample, keep at 4 °C with a magnetic stirrer set to slow continuous stirring. Add the first 50 % of solubilized sample dropwise, stir 15 min, then incubate 4 h at 4 °C. Add the remaining 50 % similarly, stir 15 min, incubate another 4 h (overnight incubation optional for optimal folding).

steps.title: Concentrate and dialyze
steps.instruction: Concentrate the folded mixture to 100–200 mL using a 5 kDa cutoff filter at 4 °C (tangential‑flow filtration preferred). Transfer to a dialysis membrane (≤20 kDa cutoff) and dialyze 2 h at 20‑22 °C against 5 L Dialysis Buffer 2 with stirring. Open the membrane, pipet up/down with a 5 mL pipette, then place on ice with 5 L Dialysis Buffer 3 and continue dialysis overnight. Change back to Dialysis Buffer 2 and dialyze another 2 h at 20‑22 °C. Centrifuge the dialyzed protein 17 500 × g ≥15 min at 4 °C and transfer to a 250 mL Schott bottle; keep at 4 °C or on ice from now on.

steps.title: Purify folded proBDNF (SP‑sepharose)
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.5 mL SP‑sepharose beads to a 30 mL gravity column, equilibrate with 12.5 mL SP‑Equilibration Buffer, remove buffer, add beads to the ~200 mL dialyzed protein, incubate ≥30 min at 4 °C with gentle stirring, return beads to the column and collect flow‑through (keep cold). Wash beads twice with 12.5 mL Wash Buffer 3. Elute with 2.5 mL SP‑Elution Buffer, incubate 10 min at 4 °C on a roller, collect eluate; repeat elution 5 more times (total 6 fractions). Store eluates on ice/4 °C and measure concentration (~0.6 mg/mL).

steps.title: Purify folded proNT4 (Ni‑NTA)
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.5 mL Ni‑NTA beads to a 30 mL gravity column, equilibrate with 12.5 mL Wash Buffer 3, remove buffer, add beads to the dialyzed protein, incubate ≥30 min at 4 °C with gentle stirring, return beads to the column and collect flow‑through (keep cold). Wash beads twice with 12.5 mL Wash Buffer 3. Elute with 2.5 mL Ni‑Elution Buffer, incubate 10 min at 4 °C on a roller, collect eluate; repeat 5 more times (6 fractions). Store eluates on ice/4 °C and measure concentration (~0.8 mg/mL).

steps.title: Desalt on NAP25 column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a NAP25 column with 4 × 5 mL Wash Buffer 3. Load 2.5 mL of each elution fraction onto the column (for proNT4 load only fractions 2–6; fraction 1 serves as a wash). Add 3.5 mL Wash Buffer 3, collect the flow‑through, pool in a 50 mL tube, measure concentration (~0.3 mg/mL), and store at 4 °C overnight or at –20 °C if processing is finished.

steps.title: Activate proBDNF with furin
steps.instruction: Add CaCl₂ to a final concentration of 5 mM, then add Furin at a mass ratio of 1:100 (Furin:neurotrophin). Incubate ≥4 h at 20‑22 °C on a roller incubator. Stop the reaction by adding EDTA to a final 10 mM (pH 7.5), then centrifuge 17 500 × g ≥10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Purify mature BDNF (SP‑sepharose)
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL SP‑sepharose beads to a 15 mL gravity column, equilibrate with 5 mL SP‑Equilibration Buffer, load the activated BDNF mixture with the column outlet closed, incubate ≥30 min at 4 °C, then collect flow‑through (keep cold). Wash beads at least five times with 10 mL Wash Buffer 3 (optional first five washes contain 1 M urea). Elute with 1 mL SP‑Elution Buffer, incubate 10 min at 4 °C on a roller, collect eluate; repeat elution 5 more times (6 fractions). Store eluates at 4 °C until buffer exchange and measure concentration (~0.2 mg/mL).

steps.title: Buffer exchange via NAP10
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a NAP10 column with 4 × 5 mL 1× PBS pH 7.4. Load 1 mL of each BDNF elution onto the column, let it enter, then add 1.5 mL 1× PBS pH 7.4 and collect the flow‑through (contains BDNF). Store BDNF at –20 °C; store NT4 at 4 °C (do not freeze). Note: Use low‑binding membranes (e.g., Sartorius Hydrosart) for any concentration steps to minimise loss; typical final yields are ~0.2 mg/mL for mature NT4 and BDNF.

description: Timing: 1–2 days This protocol describes the methodology to obtain correctly folded and disulfide-linked neurotrophins proBDNF and proNT4 from E. coli BL21(DE3) Rosetta 2 strain. However, simple BL21 (DE3) E. coli work as well. It is important to emphasize that the neurotrophins must be produced in their pro-forms even though the active forms may be required. The pro-peptides prove to fulfill critical chaperone function for proper folding.1.For one inclusion body pellet prepare 1.8 L of LB-medium (3x 600 mL in 2 L shaker flasks) in advance.a.Additionally, prepare at least 1x 50 mL LB-medium in a 250 mL flask for an inoculation culture.b.Autoclave both and let them cool down to room temperature (20°C–22°C) before inoculation with E. coli.2.Start an inoculation culture.a.Transfer the plasmids into 100 μL chemo competent BL21 (DE3) Rosetta 2 E coli.b.After the cells recovered in 500 μL LB medium, transfer the cells into the prepared 50 mL LB-medium with selection (100 μg/mL Ampicillin, 20 μg/mL Chloramphenicol).c.Grow them over night in a shaker (37°C, 200 rpm).Note: This is a polyclonal expression system! Monoclonal expression can be set up as well, by plating the recovered cells (in a dilution series) on several LB-agar plates containing 100 μg/mL Ampicillin, 20 μg/mL Chloramphenicol growing them over night. Clearly separated colonies can be picked to inoculate 5 mL LB-medium growing them over night resulting in a monoclonal starting culture.3.Prepare all buffers described in Materials and Equipment segment in advance and keep/store them at the recommended temperatures.Note: Buffers that contain urea should always be prepared freshly and kept at 4°C to minimize carbamylation.4.To measure protein concentrations throughout the whole experiment in a reliable manner it should be done with Bradford Assay. Therefore, prepare a calibration curve with i.e., BSA.Note: UV/Vis is also viable, but is significantly influenced by the L-Arginine, which is used in the folding buffer
